title: 0178 carries a wrong mechanism clause, and there is no verb that can correct an issue body
body:
**CORRECTS 0178. Its clause _Modified files are immune, which is why it took three weeks to surface_ IS FALSE, and acting on 0178 as written leaves half the class open.**

**ic FOUND IT; I REPRODUCED IT RATHER THAN RELAYING IT.** In a scratch repository: commit a base, `git add` a modification (ambient index now holds the NEW blob), move the file again, then commit that path through a private `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. After the private-index commit:

    git status --porcelain mod.txt   -> MM
    index blob f719efd4  !=  HEAD blob 2bdf67ab
    git diff --cached HEAD           -> 1 file changed, a real reverting change

**So the ambient entry survives and goes STALE, and a plain `git commit` then lands the old blob -- REVERTING THE COMMITTER'S OWN JUST-LANDED CHANGE.** Created paths lose their entry and read as a staged DELETION; modified paths keep a stale entry and read as a staged REVERSION. Two shapes, one mechanism, and only the first was in 0178.

**HOW THE WRONG CLAUSE GOT THERE, because it is a better lesson than the fact.** cc measured whether an ambient entry EXISTS -- four modified paths had one, one created path did not -- and inferred immunity from presence. **The measurement was correct and the inference was not: presence is not currency.** I filed the inference as fact without re-deriving it, which is the same move I have corrected in others twice today.

**THE REPAIR IS ic's AND IT COVERS BOTH SHAPES:** `git restore --staged -- <every committed path>` after any private-index commit, not just the created ones.

=== AND THE REASON THIS IS A SECOND ISSUE RATHER THAN AN EDIT ===

**`intent issues` HAS `add`, `list`, `show`, `close` AND `open`, AND NO `edit`. An issue body is write-once.** `intent edit <kind> <id>` does not reach one either -- every kind resolves to a steel thread, so `intent edit issue 0178` answers `no steel thread ST0178 in this project`.

**So a factual error in an issue body cannot be corrected by any verb the tool ships**, and the only available remedy is a second record that contradicts the first -- which is the many-homes defect arriving as the ONLY option rather than as a lapse. Same family as issue 0033: a field the typed API has no verb for. Post-tag, and cheap: either an `issues edit` verb, or `intent edit` accepting the kinds its own address grammar already parses (`address.rs` maps `/issues/<id>` perfectly well).
